correctness.rationale: For all R>0, alpha>1 and unequal positive initial data: exact log-ratio drift enforces preserved winning order and divergent log ratio; boundedness then forces loser extinction. Eventual small loser, growth below R/4 and a uniform upper bound prove the surviving coordinate eventually has a positive floor. Telescoped log-population equations give time average R for the winner and exact negative logarithmic rate -(alpha-1)R for the loser. At alpha=1 the ratio is invariant and the scalar total-population Ricker map persists; for alpha<1 small-R coexistence equilibrium has both multipliers strictly in the disk. Finite verification outputs support identities without replacing proof.

originality.rationale: The exact global loser exponent and its all-positive-off-diagonal validity for any log reproductive growth R>0 are not given by the 2026 local bifurcation paper, the 2022 multistability diagrams, or the inapplicable sufficient coefficient ordering of the 2015 general winner theorem. Related accessible published research on Ricker synchronous Floquet spectra and symmetric two-cycle stability addresses distinct invariant sets; qualitative competitive exclusion alone does not imply the exact all-trajectory logarithmic rate. A complete historical priority claim is not made.

value.rationale: The sharp cross-competition cutoff separates deterministic order-selected elimination from persistent coexistence possibilities even when intrinsic Ricker growth is high and irregular. The exact loser rate is universal across all positive initial states and non-equilibrium survivor dynamics, giving a quantitative extinction law distinct from local fixed-point or sampled bifurcation information.
